name: Integral point sets in general position (no three collinear, no four concyclic)
description: construct() -> {'D': D, 'points': [[[x_num, x_den], [y_num, y_den]], ...]} describing 3 to 12 distinct points (x, y*sqrt(D)) with rational x, y (|numerators|, denominators <= 10^40) and squarefree D <= 10^12. All pairwise distances must be rational (equivalently integral after scaling), no three points collinear and no four concyclic, all checked with exact rational arithmetic. Maximize the number of points. A valid set certifies such configurations of that size; 8 points would be new.

sources.locator: Tobias Kreisel and Sascha Kurz, There Are Integral Heptagons, no Three Points on a Line, no Four on a Circle (2008). Crossref record inspected; Erdős Problem #213 page inspected: Anning and Erdős excluded infinite sets, Harborth found 5 points, Kreisel and Kurz 7 points (the best construction), and 8 points remain open. Every planar integral point set has a characteristic D putting its points at (a, b*sqrt(D)) after a similarity (Kemnitz), so the representation is general. A valid set certifies such configurations of that size; 8 points would be new.
Erdős Problem #213 (open); statement, history and current bounds reviewed 2026-09-24.
JSP-000197; pinned discovery source, independently paraphrased. Primary mathematical attribution follows the papers above.
